doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: The fourth melody player and balancing egos in the Flecktones
summary: The fourth member has to fit a group that has been together sixteen years while still standing up as a strong player. Everyone in the band is a leader, and Fleck has learned to trust his instincts about the group's overview.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: player who’s willing to fit into the group and find a way to make the whole group sound good. And he’s actually the guest sort of. He shouldn’t be the dominant figure. He should be an equal fourth at best. Or right in there. Because I mean the other three guys have been together for sixteen years. He’s only been here for — I mean it’s a delicate balance. And yet he needs to come forward and be strong and be a powerful musician that can stand up there with us and be dominant as well. So it’s a very tricky position for that fourth person. It always has been ever since Howard left.
Is there a balancing of egos involved?

Absolutely. Because anybody that’s going to play with us, I mean I’ll sound like an egotistical guy, but they have to be really good musicians. They have to be strong. They have to have their own career too. They have to be a guy who has a strong leadership ability. Everyone in our group is a leader, really. So when you’ve got somebody like that they may be used to calling the shots. But that’s not really their role in that situation. I have to be that guy because I’m the guy with the overview of this particular music that we’re doing as a four piece group. Not that anybody else in the group wouldn’t have equally good input or overview on their own music, but for this stuff I have an instinct for it. And I’ve come to terms with it. And it’s been difficult for me because I’m not a dominant person in general but I’ve learned to fight for it if I think it’s not going the right way, and that my instincts are very solid about this particular version of music that we do together that’s the Flecktones. I wouldn’t say it’s better than anybody else’s as it regards the music that they’re working or even at times in our music, but as a general overview I’ve learned to trust my instincts.
